posts.content_html_raw:
My list of who's going to commit murder and why.


3. Makoto - She's just been put through the mental ringer, and while she's started the road to recovery, she's far from fine. And the fact that she's just been hit with an existential bombshell that I don't believe she's processed yet puts more pressure on already shaky ground. I can see her relapsing into depression and getting dangerous now that she knows about the loops and the lack of foreseeable consequences that they give her. I believe her murder victim will be her mom. Her and Maki haven't even begun to heal their broken relationship. And I can see her snapping during an argument with her mom.


2. Ami - If you don't know why she's on the list, then you're a goober. My money's on her first murder victim being Maya. In Ami's eyes, the biggest threat to her happiness with Akira is Maya. This is hammered home in the Halloween party, where she calls out Maya, and in the bad uncle scene with Noriko. When she snaps, the first thing that's got to go will be Maya, and speaking of Maya...


1. Maya - it's impossible to miss that she's falling apart mentally. She's not mentally strong; she's just numb to it all. And her knowledge, while it didn't give her control, gave her comfort. But all that's gone out the window, new stuff is happening and her feelings that she thought she buried are resurfacing. She can't act on her feelings; she doesn't know what's going to happen, all while Ayane rubs it in her face that she has the one thing she's been wanting for the past 1000000+ loops. She's going to snap and it's going to be brutal. My money's on Ayane being her target. Ayane will probably try not to be as boastful about banging sensei after Maya's outburst at the end of the update, but since it's Ayane, she'll still do it unintentionally and consistently. Hell, I'm pretty sure if Ami does kill Maya, then Ayane's next on the list.


Next is the list of who's going to French kiss the barrel of a gun (or other fun analogies for suicide). No numbers, because they all seem equally likely to me.


Io. Things are looking up for Io right now, but the fact that she let her wish about the relationship she wants with sensei and Uta out is what's going to break her, because she's going to get it. We've seen that she's extremely possessive even before shes in a relationship with Akira and I doubt that going to go away when Uta makes her move. When stuff starts happening between Uta and Akira, I can see Io start to harshly compare herself to Uta and in true Io fashion she'll find herself short in all categories. She'll close herself off from both Akira and Uta to try not to interfere between them. (A reversal of what's been going on.) And with nowhere to turn to, I can see Io's mind going to some dark places very quickly. Overdosing might seem like the best thing she can do to support Uta and Akira. (Extra depression points if Uta finds her while she's still conscious and dies in her arms)


Chika - Chika is probably the only girl who has strictly benefited from her relationship with Akira and is probably one of the most stable girls in the class right now. Even if she loses Akira, she's still got Chinami to keep her going, but as someone already pointed out, if she loses both, she'd probably lose the will to keep going. I can see her wasting away in depression. But I can see her pulling a Doki Doki Sayuri as well. (Extra depression points if this happens just as Chinami comes back from whatever happened to make her "disappear" and is the one to find her.)


Rin - Rin struggled with bouts of extreme depression and cutting for most of the game. But she's always kept enough sense to never cut too deep. But when we found her the second time, she admitted that she cut deeper than intended because of Otoha. Otoha also tends to go through episodes of maniacal focus, like Nodoka, and is just as hostile. If both happen to have an episode at the same time, I can see the manic Otoha getting extremely hostile if she bumps into a broken Rin and then saying some extremely hash things, pushing Rin over the edge. (Extra depression points if Rin snaps out of it after cutting herself and begins begging Otoha to help her, but Otoha's too manic to notice or care and won't realize what happened until it's far too late.)

Yeah he both does and kind of doesn't count within that event as well. Idk, it's weird. As for "Ad infinitum", It's a rather recent event which requires two conditions to be met if I recall. So, yeah, missing it is understandable.

Now as for the gods, here's my take:

Nozomu is the first god, but Nozomu in japanese translates to "Hope", and both the first god and HOPE are noted to have many eyes and be related to callousness, so they seem to be more of less the same thing. They also seem to be Yasu's god. To be frank though, "Nozomu" is "dead", and HOPE might be it reborn. User1 also seems related to that first god, mostly based off context. Also this god seems strong in Summer, and weaker in Winter.

The 2nd god is the god of wires which is also seemingly User2, and seems related to The Old District as well as maybe Tsuneyo's father. In the first Happy Event it even seems to show up with a bowl of Ramen. It's the tree like, computer like, calm god, that seems to want to protect Sensei and has the ability to reset people. Might also be who Maya asks to reset the world. This god seems stronger in Winter.

The 3rd god aka the concerned, seems to be User3, talks in lower case only, and gave it's name as "Pareidolia" in "Ad infinitum". It claims to not be on Sensei's side but wants to use him for good. It seemed to help Sana against User1 in "Ad infinitum", and helped Sensei against User1 in the Happy Event "Trinity III Non est Deus". This god doesn't have a season, but claims to be growing stronger. Like something else.

The 4th god/User4 is more or less just a mystery. It is apparently reserved.

There's also "The World" that Yasu mentions at times, like in her "The River Styx" event, which might be Sekai (Sekai translates to World in japanese), and it's said to be the last of it's kind, and has tendrils that come from the sky. Seemed excited the day Makoto's father died.

Then there's Nao which shows up in the "Mother's milk" Happy Event, which seems to be beyond the gods if not the one telling them what to do. Nao also mentions a "Spirit" that wanted to want.

Speaking of spirits, there seems to be a spirit version of Sekai wandering around doing things. Why? Not entirely sure. Then again, could just be a form "The World" is taking, some creation of Nozomu, or something on the level of Nao. Might even be User4. Not sure. Also seems to be possessing Kaori.

Overall: There's a handful of beings and it's not exactly clear what they want, what they do, or what they are, yet. This is simply how I see them at the moment.

Then there's Nao which shows up in the "Mother's milk" Happy Event, which seems to be beyond the gods if not the one telling them what to do. Nao also mentions a "Spirit" that wanted to want.
Speaking of spirits, there seems to be a spirit version of Sekai wandering around doing things. Why? Not entirely sure. Then again, could just be a form "The World" is taking, some creation of Nozomu, or something on the level of Nao. Might even be User4. Not sure. Also seems to be possessing Kaori.
Overall: There's a handful of beings and it's not exactly clear what they want, what they do, or what they are, yet. This is simply how I see them at the moment.

This is my first ever post and quite frankly I would prefer it to also be my last but honestly? I am a degenerate. I've played games spanning across many tags but so far my favorites have hit titles such as 'Corrupted Kingdoms, Harem Hotel, Drop Out, The Headmaster and others that don't make it to the point of being name dropped.

I'm not even finished with what is considered chapter one and quite frankly I've had to ask myself at least 6 times if i actually should be paying for therapy. I have cried, I have laughed inappropriately and then i have found myself back in depression.

This game literally has you experience an orgasm in it's writing and the post nut clarity that follows only to blue ball you with the inevitable outcome of your actions as the story progresses. You are awful. But the world is awful too. Praise Be. The OST is a masterpiece compared to almost any other game as well. (Don't think i can't hear Xion theme but less tempo)

I have genuinely never been so fixated on something that makes me both feel so great and so bad at the same time since I was forced to watch Evangelion or Madoka Magica. The game makes me feel like I'm Shinji jerking off on Asuka in a coma but this is a win for you since it's what you wanted the entire time.

Everything about this game hits my checklist because it's not just some random smut. Alright, time to bitch about something that doesn't fuckin' matter at all.

Ok, so in the most pedantic form of petulant pickiness, i fucking hate Io's name. See, i can totally handle short names but this one has layers of annoyance built in. I have this problem with every 2-vowels-only word in japanese. The damn phoneme compression is set to maximum on every single one of them.

Overview:
Take over as the teacher of twenty high school students as they attempt to find their way through life. Manage and develop relationships with each of them in the fictional city of Kumon-mi. Choose how to spend your time after school and on weekends to best suit the path you want to take. Whether it be visiting the girls at their part time jobs, trying to convince them to let you into their dorm rooms, or just hanging out in the room with clocks at the local bar, there is always something to do in Lessons in Love.
Please note, some things in this game may be meant to confuse or disturb you.
But don't worry! Everything will be okay~​

Back to the theory that all girls are Sensei's daughters. I don't believe in this but I think the lineage issue is really important to the plot. So, what if all the characters do share a common ancestry, but at a rather weak level? Let's say all the characters had one original ancestor (god?) and it is because of their partial divinity that they can be named characters in Kumon-mi, have the potential to survive resets, and also attract the attention, one way or another, of the current gods.
But they are all on different levels because after a lot of years and generational changes, most families' bloodlines have become too diluted, which is why they have become "blind" and weak in relation to most things in Kumon-mi. In contrast to this, the Arakawa and Sakakibara families have saved much more and because of this they can see, hear and feel the true essence of things (I also think that they are much more influential and less defenseless to mysticism than they show us - I believe that they just don’t know how to show their abilities ).

Edit: This can also explain why the main and side characters are "immortal", while the same cleaners or Makoto's father are quite mortal.

I think this possibility is more plausible.

Okay, I'll just try to mention what I consider notably important since .28, so, yeah incoming spoilers:
Sekai Related Stuff:

  • Sekai has apparently been around in Sensei's life since she played peekaboo with him when he was little.
  • Noodles, The Shapeshifter, and Black Angels seem to be related to this Sekai.
  • Sekai and her angels can make the likes of Sensei, and the girls black out then make them have sex whether they want to or not.
  • Sekai revealed she loves Ami more than Sensei, but loved him the most before her. - All of this from the japanese event that translates to Peekaboo, and the 'Toys' Futaba event for the sex stuff.
  • Noriko reminds Sensei of Sekai, and Sekai's word is law, so he either has to imagine her tongue is Sekai's or bite it off, so he seems to imagine Sekai. Also Sekai calls Sensei "Akira" but he doesn't seem to acknowledge it. - 'Smells of Summer'
  • Sekai seems to show up, scare a Narrator, and claim Yasu. - 'Shelter'
  • Sekai used Sensei as an outlet for her darkest desires when he was a kid, and eventually they both became addicted to having sex together, and fell in "love". Sekai also seems related to Nao. - 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event
  • Kaori wearing Sekai's outfit seems to have made it to the roof without anyone knowing. - 'A Thousand Years'
  • Sekai likes Nodoka, and claims Nodoka is like her, but less pretty. -'Lavender' Nodoka Event
  • Kaori doesn't seem able to acknowledge Maya, and is found staring up as it rains. - 'A brutal, violent creaming' Maya event
  • Kaori seems to be related to Sekai and possibly possessed by her. - 'Where the Trees live' Kaori event
  • Kaori may be some kind of zombie kept alive by Sekai, seeing as how in Hexadecimal Kaori mentions she doesn't understand how she's alive and her insides don't seem to work right. - 'First Contact'
godly related stuff:
  • Yasu's god seems to have skipped the past 2 months for everyone, which caused the timeline to skip from Halloween Dorm War to Beachmas.
  • Yasu seems to be trying to convince Ayane to meet her god, which will allow Ayane to replace Maya. Also her god wants to watch Sana masterbate apparently, which causes Sana to uncontrollably masterbate in a public bathroom. - 'No cumming on Christmas'
  • Yomiel, one of Yasu's bunnies, reveals that Bunnies like him are placed all over the world to learn and observe. He also seems to be falling out of favor with his designated god, Yasu's god, and wants to move towards the center god(?). Yomiel also seems terrified of Sekai. - Peekaboo event.
  • Yasu claims that Yasu's god wants Maya, and that Maya is temporary like others like her. Also birds are sacred, can walk through planes, and do/hear things. - The Legacy of Thaum part IV
  • Some kind of twisted Ami thing shows up behind Yumi and Sensei - 'A Day in the life' Yumi Event
  • Something's shadow shows up behind Sensei and Tsuneyo, the other girls go T Shaped, and Am I Okay Maya asks if Sensei has found "the Paradox" yet, in Hexadecimal - 'December 28, 2020 (Clay & Clockwork)'
  • Angels which are now Black seem to be the writers of Long Maya's children show, which can send Sensei back in time if he doesn't answer the questions correctly. The Shapeshifter also seems involved, but implies that things are out of control, yet is too scared of Long Maya filing a complaint, to not do as is asked of her. The name Ayane chose for her kid will seemingly affect the Shapeshifter's future. Something intervenes and ends the segment. - 'Untitled'
  • Nao is revealed. Looks like Ami with odd eyes, and claims to be Sensei.
  • The Wishing Well is revealed. Also known as The Library. Might be Nao's bowels. Seems to contain everything including other universes and the memories of everyone.
  • Nao mentions a "Spirit" that can be everything and wanted to want something.
  • Nao claims to experience and catalogue Sensei's experiences, to be fear itself, can be anything, has half divine actions that won't change things, seems aware of other universes, as well as those that want to use Sensei, even though Nao doesn't, and it just might as well as be nigh omnipotent. Also notes that Sensei isn't even a puzzle piece and is more comparable to a puppet or ant meant to run in circles.
  • Nao seems to be working with Sekai, and claims "We" will be watching Sensei. - All Nao and Wishing Well stuff from 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event
  • The 4th god seems to be the ultimate being and wants to be everything, according to a Narrator. Probably best to just check this out for yourself. - 'All for you'
Some other notable lore stuff:
  • Yumi, Makoto, and Tsuneyo seemed to notice the loops.
  • Tsuneyo apparently had no trouble understanding the resets and seems to feel like she's heard it before.
  • Tsuneyo notes that if memories can be altered and falsified, then Maya's memories could have as well.
  • Tsuneyo seemed unaffected by whatever caused Maya, Ayane, and Yumi to go T Shaped during the last reset. She also left when the reset happened due to some smell at Tojo Ramen.
  • Yumi and Tsuneyo seem to have failed getting to the roof anyway.
  • Pregnancy is apparently not the cause for Ayane getting to the roof.
  • Maya claims Tsuneyo doesn't seem to recall the resets now.

Well, ignoring that some of that being unrealistic even for their wealth, especially for what she'd gain, I'd largely agree.
You can SAY a character is as smart as you like, you can have them rattle off the most difficult questions you can google, or step in and say all according to plan at the end, but in practice an author can never really make a character more intelligent than themselves.
This generally isn't a big deal as long as you don't put their inner workings on full display, and that's the true crux of the problem here. We're being allowed to see a bit too much of the wizard behind the curtain regarding Tsubasa's machinations, letting us also see the holes and convolution in it.

Well, there's Chika's pride, and Touka's experience which comes into play, then Tsubasa seems to want to keep her husband from knowing about all of this, while also keeping Sensei more or less on a leash and as a potential willing servant/boy toy.

Chika isn't willing to accept that much help, so Tsubasa needs to convince her to improve their lives without forcing it upon her. Touka will be taking over one day, so her running this apartment complex will give her some experience when it comes to business and potentially love due to Sensei. Then there's Sensei, who is a love interest of Chika's, a love interest of Touka's, and a love interest of her own, but he's also a piece of shit, so this will keep him close so that she can monitor and use him as she sees fit, while giving him the necessary freedom to keep him "happy".

If Tsubasa just suddenly buys up the Old District, then there's no way that won't go unnoticed by Chika, and Tsubasa's husband. I also doubt it'd be cost effective, and it's probably not something she has interest in overall. The Old District likely wouldn't be so decrepit if the Tsukiokas gave a damn. There's also the Yakuza presence, which might come into play, making the Old District kind of a potential war zone.

I also don't think Tsubasa sees Chika or Chinami as worth that much effort in the grand scheme of things. Chika sees her as a mother figure, but Tsubasa likely doesn't see her as much more than a potentially worthwhile investment for her, and her daughter's mental health. Just like Sensei.

  • Some kind of twisted Ami thing shows up behind Yumi and Sensei - 'A Day in the life' Yumi Event
  • Something's shadow shows up behind Sensei and Tsuneyo, the other girls go T Shaped, and Am I Okay Maya asks if Sensei has found "the Paradox" yet, in Hexadecimal - 'December 28, 2020 (Clay & Clockwork)'

The Shapeshifter also seems involved, but implies that things are out of control, yet is too scared of Long Maya filing a complaint, to not do as is asked of her.   • Nao is revealed. Looks like Ami with odd eyes, and claims to be Sensei.
  • The Wishing Well is revealed. Also known as The Library. Might be Nao's bowels. Seems to contain everything including other universes and the memories of everyone.
  • Nao mentions a "Spirit" that can be everything and wanted to want something.
  • Nao claims to experience and catalogue Sensei's experiences, to be fear itself, can be anything, has half divine actions that won't change things, seems aware of other universes, as well as those that want to use Sensei, even though Nao doesn't, and it just might as well as be nigh omnipotent. Also notes that Sensei isn't even a puzzle piece and is more comparable to a puppet or ant meant to run in circles.
  • Nao seems to be working with Sekai, and claims "We" will be watching Sensei. - All Nao and Wishing Well stuff from 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event
  • The 4th god seems to be the ultimate being and wants to be everything, according to a Narrator. Probably best to just check this out for yourself. - 'All for you'
Some other notable lore stuff:
  • Yumi, Makoto, and Tsuneyo seemed to notice the loops.
  • Tsuneyo apparently had no trouble understanding the resets and seems to feel like she's heard it before.
  • Tsuneyo notes that if memories can be altered and falsified, then Maya's memories could have as well.
  • Tsuneyo seemed unaffected by whatever caused Maya, Ayane, and Yumi to go T Shaped during the last reset. She also left when the reset happened due to some smell at Tojo Ramen.
  • Yumi and Tsuneyo seem to have failed getting to the roof anyway.

  • Maya claims Tsuneyo doesn't seem to recall the resets now.
  • Yumi doesn't seem to recall the resets now.
  • Niki helped Sensei remember some of his past, including his name which is Akira.
  • Apparently Sensei seems to have just been ignoring his first name this whole time, and the likes of Noriko have been calling him Akira, but he only heard Sensei.
  • Noriko either knows about Sensei and Ami's relationship, or at least that Ami is creepily obsessive.
  • Nao-Chan seems to have shown up out of nowhere, has Ami's (or Sekai's) and Maya's eyes, and is more or less adopted by Kaori.
  • John, Kaori's chicken, is a monster or something..
  • It rains now, apparently.
  • Maya apparently spent decades to centuries trying to get Ami to acknowledge the resets but it only made her mad.
  • Ami knows how to temporarily break Sensei's mind, by mentioning her parents, and he tends to speak his thoughts unwillingly when it happens. Especially saying things like "Ami is so cute". Similar things happen to Ami, according to her.
  • Makoto told Ami about the resets.
  • Apparently If Ami finds out about the resets, she begins changing into a violent version of herself that has beaten, brutalized, and butchered everyone before the transfers in the past, according to Maya.

posts.content_html_raw:
Thoughts on this update:

1) I expected Haruka to wind up being something of a wingwoman for Akira, especially with Molly or Rin. I did not expect this. I hope we get more than one scene of this playing out. A Chika/Haruka scene is most likely because of Chika's recent ask, but man I would love to see Haruka and Makoto together. Come on, Akira, she wants to be corrupted? Make her betray her best friend by unleashing that sapphic desire upon her best friend's daughter.

2) I hope Maki doesn't figure it out until after Haruka's gone to town on Makoto as well. Largely because if shit's gonna go dark, don't half-ass it. I do appreciate the irony of Maki only finding the condoms after Makoto's decided she doesn't need them. Top notch parenting there.

3) Io saying "cock shock" got me. I liked the Yumi/Io interaction, and hope they build on that. Io needs some friends, and Yumi needs some perspective.

4)
Nao drew a thing and it came to life, and everyone she meets is all but worshipping her already. Definitely a god. I wasn't sure if the name was a red-herring coincidence or not, but that's some god-like mojo she's got there.

5) Happy scene reinforces the "Ami is dead, and our Ami is an imposter" theory, with the implication that Ami and Sekai's eyes are rotting out. This also calls the Sekai we've been seeing into question, she may not be who she looks like.

6) Touka going into mamma-bear mode over Yasu is likely going to prevent Akira from doing what Nozomu has demanded of him, so that's gonna be interesting. I feel super bad for that girl, as Nozomu has fucker her up beyond any recognition.

I expected this to be a pretty low-key update, since mega-chains tend to be high drama and we have that next month, but this was more interesting than I anticipated.

Desconstructing Metaphor

Disclaimer: I personaly don't think it is right, just throwing out my thoughts

First of all, hooray for live buildings. Strong Гигахрущ vibes

Amy implies it is Akira's origin. Other residents are numbers. Some of they are jumping (or at least thrown) into an infinte well. There is a place called Wishing Well and, AFAIR, Kumon-mi might be part of Wishing Well. Yasu also said something about reality bending in Kumon-mi, so Kumon-mi might be called "A place, where wishes literaly come true".

It also fits Maya's idea that after each reset there is new Sensei (I don't like it, but nevertheless). Also, assuming Amy never jumped, imposter Ami theory (which I don't like too) also might be true.

Given all that, Mall might be very important to understand Kumon-mi origins, even if it is not real. Because it is metaphor of something real. Amount of work involved to create it is also an inderect evidence of it's importance

Bonus

During last two patches, Selebus released some stuff which looks a bit out of place. Specificaly Psyco Ami-related events, which ended with nothing. This is first outside-of-reset puzzle, which could actualy be used during reset, especialy considering that next reset should move us to a new phase and question-style resets already exhausted themselves.

Also there is a bunch of completly forgoten side events like "Second Sun" or "Hook".

I think, Sel is rewriting chapter plot right now and we are going through old reset stuff. It's interesting, because new plot should be different frow what we seen before

with nothing
. This is first outside-of-reset puzzle, which could actualy be used during reset, especialy considering that next reset should move us to a new phase and question-style resets already exhausted themselves.
Also there is a bunch of completly forgoten side events like "Second Sun" or "Hook".
I think, Sel is rewriting chapter plot right now and we are going through old reset stuff. It's interesting, because new plot should be different frow what we seen before
